You are working in the Python repository checked out at /dateutil (dateutil library). There is a BUG in /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py. A test named `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::test_idx_check` (which is NOT in the repository) is expected to pass once the bug is fixed; the test name describes the expected behaviour (it concerns an index check in the parser). Your job: find the bug in dateutil/parser.py that makes an index-related behaviour wrong, and fix it minimally.

Approach: study dateutil/parser.py (the `_parse` method and `_timelex`), look for index arithmetic that is wrong or that can raise IndexError, and fuzz the parser to find crashes or wrong results: e.g. run many random/edge-case strings through `dateutil.parser.parse(s)`, `parse(s, fuzzy=True)`, `parse(s, fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` and look for IndexError, or for cases where a valid-looking string fails to parse. Pay special attention to the branch `elif (i == len_l and l[i-2] == ' ' and info.hms(l[i-3]) is not None)` and to the numbered-timezone branch (`res.tzoffset = int(l[i])*3600+int(l[i+2])*60`), and to the timezone-name branch. Note that the parser is expected to raise ValueError('Unknown string format') for garbage input - that is NOT a bug. An IndexError, a hang, or a wrong parse of a well-formed date string IS a bug.

Constraints: (1) Do NOT edit any test file. (2) Do NOT break existing tests: run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_parser.py -q` before and after your change and make sure the same tests pass. (3) Make the smallest possible change. (4) If you cannot find a definite bug, do not change anything.

Report: the exact bug found (file, line, code before/after), why it is a bug, the evidence (commands and outputs), and the test results before/after. If you found nothing, say so clearly.

You are working in the Python repository checked out at /dateutil (dateutil library). There is a BUG in /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py. A test named `dateutil.test.test_relativedelta.RelativeDeltaTest::testAbsoluteAddition` (which is NOT in the repository) is expected to pass once the bug is fixed; the test name describes the expected behaviour: addition involving the ABSOLUTE fields of relativedelta (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, weekday). Your job: find the bug in dateutil/relativedelta.py that makes absolute addition behave wrongly, and fix it minimally.

Approach: read /dateutil/dateutil/relativedelta.py carefully (especially `__add__`, `__radd__`, `__sub__`, `__neg__`, `_fix`, `normalized`, and the constructor). Test things like: `datetime(2000,1,15) + relativedelta(day=1)`, `relativedelta(day=1) + relativedelta(day=2)`, `relativedelta(hour=5) + relativedelta(minute=30)`, `relativedelta(month=2) + datetime(2000,1,31)`, `relativedelta(day=1) + datetime(2000,1,15)`, `relativedelta(weekday=MO) + datetime(...)`, and combinations of absolute and relative fields. Compare against the documented algorithm in the class docstring (steps 1-7) and against the behaviour of `datetime.replace` + timedelta arithmetic. Look for a subtly wrong operator, a wrong variable, or a wrong fallback (e.g. `self.x or other.x` vs `other.x or self.x`, `or` vs `is not None`).

Constraints: (1) Do NOT edit any test file. (2) Do NOT break existing tests: run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_relativedelta.py -q` before and after, and also `python -m pytest dateutil -q` at the end; the same tests must pass (62 pass in test_relativedelta.py at the start). (3) Make the smallest possible change. (4) If you cannot find a definite bug, do not change anything.

Report: the exact bug found (file, line, code before/after), why it is a bug, evidence (commands and outputs), and test results before/after. If you found nothing, say so clearly.
